key_insight: Random data splits can reward recipe memorisation, while provenance-grouped evaluation better tests generalisation to unseen perovskite solar-cell research.
engineering_relevance: Reliable device optimisation requires models that generalise across research institutions and account for fabrication methods and device architecture, not just absorber chemistry.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Group evaluation splits to isolate duplicate devices, publications and institutions.
Benchmark 13 models and examine feature importance.
evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another; tree ensembles lead on random splits, but composition-aware neural models excel on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
watch_item: Implementing the protocol requires reliable recipe matching and provenance metadata; the abstract does not report numerical performance gains.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
